speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help me understand the severity and cause, have you noticed any numbness in your hand or fingers, and does this weakness affect your ability to grip objects?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of anabolic steroid use, diabetes, and recent significant weight loss, could you describe exactly which muscles in your right arm are most affected by the weakness? Additionally, have you noticed any muscle wasting (shrinking) in your forearm or shoulder compared to the other side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Paraneoplastic Amyotrophy (Parsonage-Turner Syndrome) secondary to an underlying malignancy.

The combination of progressive proximal muscle weakness, sensory loss, burning pain, significant weight loss, and your history of heavy smoking and anabolic steroid use strongly suggests an underlying cancer causing a paraneoplastic syndrome. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest, CT_Abdomen, CT_Pelvis to screen for a primary tumor. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Right_Arm to assess for muscle atrophy and nerve involvement.
